title: Sell Mineral Rights in Charleroi, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Charleroi, PA | Washington County
metaDescription: Charleroi sits on Marcellus wet-gas ground in Washington County. We buy mineral and royalty interests directly from PA owners, including small fractional shares.
heroLead: Charleroi grew up on the Monongahela River around glass factories, not gas wells, but the ground underneath the borough and the farmland around it sits in Washington County's wet-gas core.
intro: We hear from a fair number of owners in Charleroi whose mineral interest isn't tied to a farm at all. It came down through a family that worked the glass plants or the mills, bought a house lot generations ago, and the mineral rights just rode along with the deed, unnoticed until a landman or a royalty statement showed up. That's a different situation than a working farm family selling off part of what feeds them, and we treat it that way.

Washington County has been one of the most active counties in the whole Marcellus play for over a decade, which means Charleroi-area interests, even small in-town parcels, sometimes carry real value. We buy them outright, in cash, without asking you to list anything or wait on a broker.

sections.heading: River Borough, Core Wet-Gas Ground
paragraphs: Charleroi itself is a dense river borough, but the townships around it, especially toward Fallowfield and Carroll, sit squarely in Range Resources and EQT operating areas. Wet gas here means higher liquids content in the produced stream, which has historically supported stronger economics than dry-gas acreage further northeast, though that always depends on current prices, not a fixed multiple we'd quote you upfront.

If your interest is under a residential lot rather than open farmland, it can still be part of a larger drilling unit. Units get drawn by the operator across many parcels, and a small in-town tract can be pooled right alongside the surrounding farms.

sections.heading: Inherited Interests From Mill and Mine Families
paragraphs: A lot of the mineral ownership around Charleroi traces back to families who worked at the glass plants, the coal mines nearby, or the steel operations along the Mon Valley. Those original purchases often included the mineral rights as a matter of course, since severed sales weren't the norm in a dense borough the way they were on farmland. Over three or four generations, that interest can end up split among cousins who've never met, each holding a sliver too small to matter much individually but real all the same.
We're used to buying these small, splintered shares. If your interest is a quarter or an eighth of what your great-grandfather owned, we can still make an offer on it.

sections.heading: Checking Your Statement Against Act 13
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Act 13 impact fee is separate from your royalty and gets paid by the operator to the county and municipality, not deducted from your check, but plenty of owners confuse the two when their statement looks lower than expected. If you're not sure whether what's coming off your check is post-production costs, a Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act adjustment, or something else, send it to us and we'll tell you straight what we're looking at.

faqs.question: Does my in-town lot in Charleroi count as mineral rights, even though it's not a farm?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the deed reserved or conveyed the minerals separately, it doesn't matter whether the surface is a house lot or a hayfield. What matters is what the recorded deed actually says.

faqs.question: Is Charleroi in an active drilling area?
faqs.answer: Washington County overall has seen heavy Marcellus wet-gas activity for years, and Charleroi-area townships fall within that footprint, though specific unit activity varies parcel by parcel.

faqs.question: I only own a small fraction, is it even worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often yes. We regularly buy fractional interests as small as an eighth or a sixteenth, especially in an active county like Washington.
